channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Major fire breaks out in Alberta after deadly incident at military base
item.description: Canada’s defense minister says that people have been killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire

item.title: Dems lead GOP in House vote choice as Trump's approval rating hits record low: Poll
item.description: Half or more Americans call every household purchase category measured "unaffordable."

item.title: 2 dead, 11 injured after Kansas mother drives onto soccer field during game: Police
item.description: A child and an adult were killed after a vehicle drove through a soccer game in Wichita, Kansas Saturday afternoon, police said.

item.title: Rubio says Trump to 'analyze' global impact of Russia sanctions during pause
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia would last 60 days, as the move drew bipartisan criticism and raised fears in Ukraine that Washington could ease further restrictions on Moscow.

item.title: ‘Standing up for democracy’: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally draws Trump critics ahead of midterms
item.description: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta, one of many organised across the US on Saturday. While many demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, organisers said the rally was aimed at getting out the vote in the November 3 midterm elections and protecting democracy in America.

item.title: NHS faces 'more challenging' winter after summer of heatwaves, minister warns
item.description: The NHS faces a "more challenging" winter than normal after this summer's record-breaking heat, the health secretary has warned.

item.title: Looters seize on massive French protests to raid and vandalise shops
item.description: Looters on Saturday seized the opportunity to raid and vandalise a host of shops and businesses across France – from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores – as hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest higher living costs and other grievances.

item.title: Crush at religious festival kills at least 17 and injures dozens in India
item.description: At least 17 people have died and dozens more are injured after a crush at a religious festival in India, local media reports.

item.title: Trump waives Graham Act sanctions on Russia, drawing backlash from some lawmakers
item.description: The new sanctions and tariffs were set to take effect in two days.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats and French mayor in West Bank, Belgium says
item.description: Israeli settlers have allegedly attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the West Bank, sparking international condemnation.

item.title: India: Police crack down on New Delhi protests
item.description: Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, ‌who was detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.

item.title: Brazil: Amazon deforestation at 40-year low
item.description: In Brazil, deforestation in the Amazon has reached its lowest level in 40 years. President Lula is bolstering his environmental record just over a week before the second round of the presidential election, in which he faces Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Ukraine war: "Mothers of Kherson" opera opens in Poland
item.description: "Mothers of Kherson" has opened at Poland's National Opera. The performance was co-produced with New York's Metropolitan Opera and created in close association with Save Ukraine, a group helping to bring back Ukrainian children who remain in Russia. More than four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the opera aims to "reawaken" global interest in the war.

item.title: Protests in France: "Two fires broke out in Place de la République"
item.description: Police and protesters clashed in Paris and other French cities on Saturday, with smoke from fires and tear gas filling the air at demonstrations nationwide against high prices, ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. "Two fires broke out in Place de la République," reports France 24's Antonia Kerrigan from the ground.

item.title: More NHS staff sacked after accessing medical records of Nottingham attack victims
item.description: A total of 15 NHS staff have now been sacked after accessing medical records belonging to the victims of the 2023 Nottingham attack.

item.title: US: Four killed in Oregon school shooting
item.description: The teenage gunman who shot dead three children and a teacher in an Oregon school was a former special needs student there, officials said Friday, as they praised the heroism of people who helped to shorten the rampage.

item.title: Protests in France: "Living conditions are too harsh"
item.description: Saturday’s mobilisation in France follows calls on social media to revive the Yellow Vests movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join. We discuss this with our journalist on the ground, Antonia Kerrigan, and our guest, Paul Smith, head of Modern Languages at the University of Nottingham.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: France: What's different about today's protests?
item.description: In France, protests are under way across the country this Saturday. Demonstrators are protesting against the high cost of living, as well as poor working and studying conditions. We discuss this with France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack European delegation convoy in West Bank, beat French mayor
item.description: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy carrying a European delegation in the occupied West Bank, beating up a 78-year-old French mayor. While Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – who is just days from a crucial election – described the incident as a "smear" campaign against Israeli settlers, France's top diplomat urged Israel to "urgently halt criminal violence".

item.title: France: "We've seen extremely high tensions between protesters and law enforcement"
item.description: Protesters across France called for street demonstrations on Saturday against rising living costs. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from Paris. "The march from here to Place de Clichy isn't set to start for another hour. However, we've seen it kicking off extremely early doors. It seems that what's happened is that police attempted to block the protesters from reaching Place de la République, and we saw the use of tear gas. We've seen people running with their masks on. We also saw the use of stun grenades."

item.title: France: Students, unions and Yellow Vests unite against austerity
item.description: 190 000 people could demonstrate this Saturday in France. They called for street demonstrations Saturday against rising living costs, joining high school students' grievances over education conditions after more than three weeks of school blockades.

item.title: WATCH: David's Bridal puppy collection
item.description: Wedding retailer David’s Bridal is unveiling its new Puppy Love collection, revealing what the best-dressed best friend will wear at a pet parent’s wedding.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
item.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

item.title: Man and woman charged with assault and criminal damage after fatal house fire
item.description: A man and a woman have been charged with assault and criminal damage after a fatal house fire in Waterford, Ireland, that killed four members of the same family.

item.title: Will Paramount’s creation of Skydance test France’s cultural exception?
item.description: Skydance’s $110 billion creation tests whether France’s cultural exception can still compel a leveraged global media giant to fund, protect and prioritise French creativity, or merely treat it as a compliance cost.

item.title: Daniel Dubois retains his WBO title against Fabio Wardley
item.description: Daniel Dubois has retained his WBO world title after beating Fabio Wardley in their rematch at the O2 Arena.

item.title: Katie Zacharia 'transitioning out' of press secretary role, sources tell ABC News
item.description: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is “transitioning out” of her role, multiple sources and a senior White House official told ABC News on Friday.

item.title: Fires and clashes rock France amid massive nationwide protests
item.description: Protesters clashed with police in Paris and other French cities on Saturday as hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest higher living costs and the declining conditions in schools and other public services. Several town halls were broken into – and in at least one instance set on fire – and many shops were vandalised and ransacked. One protester had his hand torn off by what appeared to be a crowd-control grenade used by police.

item.title: Perspective: Midterm money madness
item.description: Campaign ad spending has topped $10 billion this election cycle, as voters struggle to afford groceries and gas.

item.title: France faces day of cost-of-living protests
item.description: French authorities detained dozens on Saturday at the start of nationwide protests against the cost of living, in what is likely to be a key indicator of the social climate heading toward elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs'
item.description: A dozen people were killed Saturday during a "brutal" attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

item.title: Cameroonian journalist shot in Bamenda
item.description: Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in the north-western city of Bamenda. A young woman was also killed as the attackers opened fire on mourners attending a wake. The shooting has renewed concerns about the dangers facing journalists in Cameroon's English-speaking regions, after years of conflict between government forces and separatist groups.

item.title: Uganda launches Ebola vaccine trial
item.description: The town of Masaka in southern Uganda is currently conducting a Phase 1 trial of a vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is circulating in the region. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for this strain.

item.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
item.description: More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.

item.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, contact tracing continues
item.description: Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The health ministry said the 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine, where she has been since 5 October. The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as 'historic'
item.description: Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump's move to waive new sanctions on it as "historic", as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow's side in Europe's worst conflict since World War II.

item.title: Pope Leo leaves hospital after lung cancer surgery, the Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo has left hospital, four days after his lung cancer surgery.

item.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
item.description: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

item.title: WATCH: Rhode Island farmer sets new record for world's biggest pumpkin
item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.title: Two dead after light aircraft crash
item.description: An 80-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy have died after a light aircraft crashed in Scotland, police have said.

item.title: Three men sentenced to more than 158 years in jail for murders of surfers​
item.description: Three men have been sentenced to 158 years and nine months each for the murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend.

item.title: Trump administration threatens to prosecute local California election workers
item.description: The DOJ sued over claims the state hasn't purge noncitizens from voter rolls.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: How Elon Musk is bankrolling GOP’s hopes in Texas Senate race
item.description: New campaign finance filings show the major role billionaire Elon Musk is playing in bankrolling GOP efforts against Democrat James Talarico in Texas.

item.title: New York Democrats want parking lot owners to ban ICE from their properties
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and top New York Democrats are urging private parking lot owners to block federal immigration officers from using their properties

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo's 'Moment on the Earth' spotlights the wonders of elephants
item.description: National Geographic shares a closer look at elephants, including how they can eat up to 18 hours a day and even use their trunks to "hug." "Secrets of the Elephants" is streaming now.

item.title: Trump administration accused of fast-tracking migrant children's asylum cases
item.description: Immigrant advocacy groups have sued the Trump administration to stop what they call a "cruel and unlawful scheme" to fast-track migrant children's asylum cases.

item.title: WATCH: Aboard USS George Washington as tensions rise in the Middle East
item.description: ABC News is aboard the USS George Washington near the Strait of Hormuz with rare front-line access as President Donald Trump weighs expanded operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says she did not pass bar exam
item.description: Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer; Trump called her "an attorney."

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks, Broncos face off in Thursday night NFL matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Omar Ruiz previews the Seahawks-Broncos showdown in Denver, including how Seattle’s top-ranked defense could challenge Bo Nix and whether Sam Darnold can bounce back after two interceptions.

item.title: WATCH: Rising number of young adults living with parents
item.description: ABC News’ Juju Chang reports on the growing trend of “boomerang kids” returning to live with their parents amid housing costs and financial concerns.

item.title: WATCH: DIY Halloween costumes for this year’s viral trends
item.description: Lori Bergamotto shares easy, last-minute DIY Halloween costume ideas inspired by the people and pop culture moments that made headlines this year.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir hears from Georgia firefighters who helped deliver 15 puppies
item.description: Firefighters in Cobb County answered an emergency call to help a veterinary hospital deliver 15 puppies after a rescue dog came to the local animal hospital.

item.title: WATCH: Aggressive great white shark seen off Southern California coast
item.description: Experts say the shark could be hunting for seals.

item.title: WATCH: How to navigate rising prices this holiday season
item.description: ABC News’ Elizabeth Schulze reports on what to know about the latest inflation report and prices this coming holiday season.
